mcqs.learning_point: Using classification to identify suitable materials
mcqs.question: A child wants to make a spoon that will not melt when used to stir hot soup. Which material should be chosen based on classification by the property of heat resistance?
mcqs.explanation: Metal has a high melting point and does not melt when exposed to the heat of hot soup, unlike plastic, wood, or paper which can deform or burn. Therefore, classifying materials by heat resistance points to metal as the suitable choice.

mcqs.question: You need to sort a collection of objects into two groups for a science project: those that float on water and those that sink. Which property should you select for classification?
mcqs.explanation: Whether an object floats or sinks depends on its density relative to water. Objects with lower density than water float, while those with higher density sink. Color, size, and texture do not determine buoyancy.

mcqs.question: If you group objects only by their color, which statement is true?

options.A: All objects in the same group will be made of the same material.
options.B: Objects in the same group may be made of different materials but share the same color.
options.C: Objects in the same group will all have the same weight.
options.D: Objects in the same group will all conduct electricity.

mcqs.answer: Objects in the same group may be made of different materials but share the same color.
mcqs.explanation: Grouping by a single property such as color does not guarantee similarity in material, weight, or electrical conductivity. Different materials (e.g., metal, plastic, wood) can be painted the same color, so only the color is common.

mcqs.learning_point: Creating groups using more than one property
mcqs.question: Which of the following groupings uses more than one property to classify the objects?

options.B: Objects that are both heavy and magnetic.

mcqs.answer: Objects that are both heavy and magnetic.
mcqs.explanation: Option B requires two properties—weight (heavy) and magnetism—to place an object in the group. The other options rely on a single property: material type, transparency, or color.

mcqs.learning_point: Explaining why a material belongs to a group
mcqs.question: Copper and rubber are being compared to decide which belongs to the group of electrical conductors. Why does copper belong to this group?

options.A: Because it has a high melting point.
options.B: Because it allows electricity to flow easily.

mcqs.answer: Because it allows electricity to flow easily.
mcqs.explanation: Materials are classified as conductors if they permit the easy flow of electric current. Copper’s atomic structure provides free electrons that move readily, making it an excellent conductor. The other attributes are not criteria for electrical conductivity.

mcqs.learning_point: Using classification to identify suitable materials
mcqs.question: A municipal engineer must choose a material for water pipes that will not corrode and must remain flexible under pressure. Which material is most suitable based on classification by corrosion resistance and flexibility?
mcqs.explanation: Rubber (or flexible plastic) resists corrosion and can bend without breaking, making it ideal for water pipes that need flexibility. Copper and iron can corrode over time, and glass is rigid and brittle.

mcqs.question: Which property is most useful to separate materials into conductors and insulators?
mcqs.explanation: Conductors and insulators are distinguished by their ability to allow electric current to pass. Electrical conductivity directly measures this ability, whereas color, hardness, and taste are unrelated properties.

mcqs.question: If you group objects by magnetism, which of the following items will be placed in the same group?
mcqs.explanation: Magnetism groups together objects that are attracted to a magnet. An iron nail is magnetic, while plastic, wood, and glass are not, so only the iron nail belongs in the magnetic group.
